trigger: 64 compressed packets can be submitted before an asynchronous hardware pipeline produces its first frame. The old replay-limit branch immediately selected native fallback, even without a decoder failure.
implementation_review: Replay limits remain 64 packets and 8 MiB; budget exhaustion stops hardware feeding and retains the next original packet separately as input_pending.
One monotonic first_frame_wait_started value is retained until progress, flush, or fallback; each remaining-time calculation uses that same start.
Each requested backend pull is at most 1000 ms and at most the rounded remaining progress budget; nonpositive remaining time triggers ETIMEDOUT fallback.
On first-frame success, clear_replay does not clear input_pending. The next packet-fetch branch uses the retained input instead of overwriting it with ff_decode_get_packet.
On timeout, packet 65 has not been cloned and input_in_replay is false. Native fallback replays the saved 64 originals and then consumes the retained packet 65 exactly once.

executed_tests.runner: Actual candidate ARM64 shared libraries under qemu-aarch64-static; exported stub client, no socket or devices.
executed_tests.delayed_first_frame: All zero-timeout polls remain empty for 64 accepted packets. Only the third bounded pull produces a frame. Final 65 output frames and 65 submissions have exact ordered timestamps without duplication or loss.
executed_tests.eos_regression: Both 45-frame H264 and HEVC fixtures retain the drain-error fallback/native-output comparison.
executed_tests.prior_regressions: DTS omission, ordinary-RAM pool lifetime, parameter bootstrap/no-duplication and all prior fallback tests remain included.

timing_boundary: Five seconds is the decoder-progress budget. The existing client socket receive/send timeout is separately 15 seconds per I/O wait; an unresponsive broker or stalled transport can exceed a five-second total wall-clock duration. The real-time QEMU test uses a responsive stub and measures the five-second progress branch, not a socket outage.
limits: This validates the startup race handling and exact native replay, not actual Bilibili hardware compatibility.
Actual v4 Bilibili capture already contained complete VPS/SPS/PPS; missing parameter sets is not established as its root cause.
Private capture and proprietary libraries are not uploaded publicly.
No board operation, broker restart or DMA allocation was performed by this audit.
